title: Global trends of pandemic-prone and epidemic-prone disease outbreaks in 2024
snippet: Dengue, the second disease with the most outbreaks in 2024, with 95 recorded cases, saw a 58.3% increase from 2023. While the Americas continued to report the largest absolute number of dengue-associated events (46), the most substantial year-on-year increases occurred outside the region. Africa registered two times as many outbreaks as in 2023 (20 outbreaks in 2024), and Asia recorded a 150% rise (15 outbreaks in 2024). Oceania and Europe, which had reported no dengue outbreaks in 2023, [...] Liberia, Mali, Mayotte, Niger, Réunion and Senegal. Several subregions that had not reported dengue outbreaks in 2023—including Polynesia, Melanesia, Micronesia, Australia and New Zealand, Eastern Asia and Western Europe—registered events in 2024. Conversely, Northern Africa and Northern America showed no substantial changes. Latin America and the Caribbean exhibited a relatively modest increase of 4.65%, with additional countries and territories, such as Bonaire Sint Eustatius and Saba, Chile, [...] and Saba, Chile, Cuba, Curaçao and the US Virgin Islands, reporting outbreaks in 2024, after not having reported any in the previous year. Between January and December 2024, the WHO Global Dengue Dashboard reported over 14 million cases of dengue and more than 10 500 associated deaths.6

title: Ongoing Risk of Dengue Virus Infections and Updated Testing Recommendations in the United States | HAN | CDC
snippet: Globally, dengue cases have increased substantially in the last 5 years, with the most pronounced increases occurring in the Americas. In the Americas region, 4.6 million cases and 2,400 deaths were reported in 2023, followed by 13 million cases and 8,200 deaths in 2024. As of March 6, more than 760,000 dengue cases have been reported in 2025, which is a 15% increase compared to the previous 5-year average. Epidemics in the Americas region are expected to increase both travel-associated cases [...] In the continental United States in 2024, locally acquired cases were reported in Florida (91), California (18), and Texas (1). A record number of dengue cases were identified among U.S. travelers (3,483 cases), which is an 84% increase compared to the previous year. This trend is expected to continue with increased dengue activity in endemic areas in 2025. The highest numbers of travel-associated cases in 2024 were reported in Florida (1,016) followed by California (648), and New York (327). [...] In Puerto Rico, reported dengue cases have remained above the outbreak threshold since February 2024. A public health emergency was declared in March 2024 and remains in effect. In 2024, 6,291 cases were reported, more than 52% (3,292) required hospitalization and there were 13 deaths. As of March 7, 2025, 936 cases have been reported, representing a 113% increase compared to the same period in 2024.

title: Dengue
snippet:
In 2024, more cases of dengue were recorded than ever before in a 12-month period, affecting over 100 countries on all continents. During 2024, ongoing transmission, combined with an unexpected spike in dengue cases, resulted in a historic high of over 14.6 million cases and more than 12 000 dengue-related deaths reported. The Region of the Americas contributed a significant proportion of the global burden, with over 13 million cases reported to WHO. [...] Global burden

The incidence of dengue has grown dramatically worldwide in recent decades, with the number of cases reported to WHO increasing from 505 430 cases in 2000 to 14.6 million in 2024. The vast majority of cases are asymptomatic or mild and self-managed, and hence the actual numbers of dengue cases are under-reported. The disease is now endemic in more than 100 countries. # Dengue

## Key facts

## Overview

Dengue (break-bone fever) is a viral infection that is spread from mosquitoes to people. It is more common in tropical and subtropical than in temperate climates.
